Which integral gives the area of the finite region bounded by $y=2{x}^{2}$ and $y=x+1,$ as shown above?

*(Note: Figure not drawn to scale)*
worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the intersection points between the two graphs occur when $x=-\frac{1}{2}$ and $x=1.$ So these will be our limits of integration.

To determine which is the lower function and which is the upper, let's draw our vertical arrow.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14013841/assets/e77170aac6d81b1cfd0e93804b0c59802f28089d24aeaff065da04cabc44c172.png)

The vertical line 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y=2{x}^{2},$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=x+1.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{-1/2}^{1}[\,(\text{upper function})-(\text{lower function})\,]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1/2}^{1}[\,(x+1)-(2{x}^{2})\,]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1/2}^{1}(x+1-2{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
